MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE

  Tuesday, January 25, 2022

1.  The  City Council Meeting was opened  to the public.  In an effort to keep a safe environment and to minimize the
  spread of the COVID- 19 Virus, the City limited occupancy and required masking for those in attendance.
2.  A special meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 10: 32 a.m.
3.  Council Members present:  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Muir Davis
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Absent:  Council Member Robin Carder
  Council Member Wendy Lau

  Advisory  personnel  present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  Assistant City Clerk Lupe Gaeta Estrella
  Public Works Director Shawn Igoe

4.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Pro Tem Davis.

5.  Ratifying Local Emergency Due  City Manager Russi reported on Resolution No. 22- 05, ratifying local
  to Damage Caused  emergency due to damage
  caused  by windstorm.  He stated that on Saturday,
  by
  Windstorm  January 22, 2022, acting as Director of Emergency Services he proclaimed the
  existence of a local emergency pursuant to Section 2. 56. 050 of the La Verne
  Municipal Code due to substantial wind damage throughout the City on Friday,
  2022. He stated that the
  January 21, 2022 through Saturday, January 22,
  damaging conditions are beyond the control of the services, personnel,
  equipment, and facilities of the City of La Verne and it warrants the need for
  City Council to ratify the local emergency.

  Public Works Director Igoe updated the City Council on the windstorm
  damages to the City. He stated that the City lost approximately 50 trees from
  this single event which closed several streets, sidewalks and parks, in addition
  to causing  power  outages  throughout  the City.  The Public Works Department
  has received approximately 100 service calls pertaining to damage caused by
  the windstorm. Staff continues to prioritize these requests based on safety and
  access. Cleanup efforts are anticipated to be completed in February with some
  work such as sidewalk replacement and tree planting to be completed in the
  months to follow.

  In addition, Public Works Director Igoe reported that bins have been placed at
  Fire Station 3, Mills and Kuns Parks to assist residents for disposal of green
  25tn

  waste  as  of  Tuesday January

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  There was  none.
   City Council Minutes of a Special Meeting, Tuesday, January 25, 2022, Page 2,

  The City Council commended and thanked the Public Works Crew who worked
  especially Battalion Fire Chief
  throughout the night, the Fire Department,
  Russell, La Verne Police Department and other public agencies for their
  outstanding job during a trying time.

  It was moved by Crosby, seconded  by Davis, and carried by a vote of 3- 0
  Carder and Lau Absent) to approve Resolution No. 22- 05,  ratifying the local
  emergency due to damages  caused  by  windstorm,  as follows:

  Resolution No. 22- 05,  Resolution No. 22- 05 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF LA VERNE, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA,
  Ratifying the Existence of a
  Local Emergency Regarding  RATIFYING THE EXISTENCE OF A LOCAL EMERGENCY REGARDING
  Windstorm Damages  WINDSTORM DAMAGES.

6.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment.

  There was none.

7.  Adjournment at 10: 43 a. m.

  Respectfully submitted,

  C.  J. -  t

  Lupe Gaeta Estrella, CMC
  Assistant City Clerk
